data.title: Judge puts off decision on Charlie Kirk murder trial date, media reports
data.description:
By Andrew Hay

A Utah judge on Friday said he needed more time to decide when to start the trial of Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk more than a year ago, media reported.

At a hearing in Provo, Utah, District Court Judge Tony Graf heard arguments from defense lawyers, prosecutors and a lawyer for Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk, before saying he needed to consider their positions. He set a new hearing for November 9, television station KUTV reported.

Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to seven counts, including aggravated murder, for allegedly shooting Kirk as he held one of his trademark debates at Utah Valley University in Orem. Robinson's lawyers expect a six-to-seven-month trial.

Robinson's attorneys had asked for a late 2029 trial to give them time to challenge Utah's request for the death penalty, gather additional evidence and seek a change of venue, among other issues, according to a scheduling memo.

Prosecutors, meanwhile, sought a date of January 31, 2028 to start what they expect to be a 17-week trial, according to their scheduling memo.

In a separate filing, Erika Kirk said the defense request was "grossly out of line with comparable cases" and requested the trial start no later than October 4, 2027.

Shortly before Friday's hearing, President Donald Trump, with whom Kirk had been allied, slammed Graf's handling of the case in a social media post, saying it should be tried within a month and Graf was asking "questions that people already know the answer to."

Kirk was a polarizing figure in US politics. He was admired by conservatives for mobilizing young voters around his Christian and right-wing views. Opponents criticized his rhetoric on immigration, race, gender and other social issues.

Prosecutors allege Robinson targeted Kirk for his opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights.

Defense attorney Richard Novak has said Kirk spoke "hatefully" about people who did not have traditional gender identities or were not heterosexual, but there was no evidence Robinson opposed those views.

data.title: Unbuzzd Wellness Announces Closing of Private Placement Financing
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 23, 2026) - Unbuzzd Wellness Inc. (the "Company" or "Unbuzzd"), the company behind unbuzzd™, is pleased to announce that it has completed its non-brokered private placement financing (the "Offering") in two tranches for aggregate gross proceeds of $1,080,000 through the issuance of an aggregate of 5,400,000 common shares in the share capital of the Company (the "Shares") at a price of $0.20 per Share.

The Company closed the first tranche of the Offering on October 16, 2026, issuing 2,250,000 Shares for gross proceeds of $450,000, and closed the second and final tranche on October 21, 2026, issuing 3,150,000 Shares for gross proceeds of $630,000.

In connection with the Offering, the Company paid aggregate cash commissions of $67,376 to certain finders and issued an aggregate of 327,000 non-transferable compensation common share purchase warrants (the "Compensation Warrants"). Each Compensation Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one Share at an exercise price of $0.20 per Share for a period of 24 months from its date of issuance.

The Company intends to use the proceeds from the Offering for general working capital purposes, including its application to list the Shares for trading on the Canadian Securities Exchange, which is currently under review. The Shares issued under each tranche of the Offering are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the applicable date of issuance pursuant to National Instrument 45-106 - Prospectus Exemptions.

Two insiders of the Company subscribed for an aggregate of 2,000,000 Shares under the Offering. The insider participation constitutes a "related party transaction" within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company relied on the exemption from the formal valuation requirement contained in section 5.5(b) of MI 61-101 on the basis that the Company is not listed on a specified market, and on the exemption from the minority shareholder approval requirement contained in section 5.7(1)(a) of MI 61-101 on the basis that neither the fair market value of the securities issued to the participating insiders nor the consideration paid by them exceeded 25% of the Company's market capitalization. The Company did not file a material change report at least 21 days before the closing of the applicable tranche because the details of the insider participation were not finalized until closer to closing and the Company wished to close the Offering as soon as practicable for sound business reasons.

The securities offered have not been registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from the registration requirements. This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy, nor shall there be any sale of the securities in any state in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

ABOUT UNBUZZD WELLNESS INC.

Unbuzzd Wellness Inc., a non-trading but fully reporting public issuer, stands as a pioneering force in the wellness and recovery supplement landscape. unbuzzd has been developed by a world-class R&D team in pharmacology and medicine, with a commitment to innovation and quality. A proprietary blend of vitamins, minerals, and herbs, unbuzzd helps your body process alcohol faster, restore mental alertness, and improve cognition so you can drink responsibly and drink refreshingly. unbuzzd appeals to a broad target audience of alcohol consumers who want to have a good time, be in control, and still feel great the next day.

Scientifically backed by a recently completed double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover design clinical trial, unbuzzd dramatically accelerates alcohol metabolism, speeds the reduction of blood alcohol concentration ("BAC"), restores mental clarity, and reduces the symptoms of intoxication, impairment and hangover. Key findings from the clinical trial include:

  • Accelerated Alcohol Metabolism: unbuzzd dramatically and rapidly reduced blood alcohol concentration in study participants. The rate at which BAC was lowered was, on average for most participants, more than 40 percent faster within 30 minutes of consuming unbuzzd compared to control subjects.
  • Rapid Improvements in Alertness: Study participants reported statistically significant improvement in alertness as soon as 30 minutes after consuming unbuzzd. Participants felt more alert and made fewer cognitive errors within 30 minutes of consuming unbuzzd, significantly outperforming placebo results.
  • Rapid Improvements in Physiologic Changes due to Intoxication: unbuzzd lessened the elevation in heart rate and the drop in blood pressure that often accompanies alcohol intoxication, stabilizing both. This result was statistically significant.
  • Reduced Perceived Impairment and Mental Fatigue: unbuzzd helped alleviate perceived impairment and mental fatigue caused by alcohol intoxication.
  • Hangover Relief: Participants in this study noted a statistically significant reduction in hangover symptoms. This included reduced cognitive and physical impairment, and reduced headache compared to placebo results, at both four hours (67 percent reduction in headache severity) and eight hours after consuming unbuzzd.
  • No Side Effects: unbuzzd was well-tolerated by all study participants, with no reported adverse side effects.

data.title: Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, CEO Jassy says
data.description:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on Friday that Amazon Web Services' cloud computing capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with significant commitments extending into 2028, on growing demand for AI infrastructure.

In a video podcast with Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz and general partner Erik Torenberg, Jassy said Amazon is struggling to keep pace with the insatiable demand from AI labs and enterprises.

  • Earlier this year, Amazon had said it would spend about $220 billion in capital expenditure for 2026

  • Jassy said the company "could invest a lot more and it wouldn't be a bad use of capital," considering cloud-computing capacity for 2026 is already sold out

  • "2027 is largely sold out. We always leave a certain amount for on demand and our inference service bedrock, or EC2, but largely sold out all the big chunks. A good chunk of 2028 is sold out," he said

  • EC2 is an AWS service that provides cloud servers for running applications, while Bedrock gives customers access to AI models to build generative AI applications

  • Amazon is scheduled to report third quarter results on October 29

data.title: Moderna's Cancer Vaccine Success Doesn't Live Up to Early Hype — WSJ
data.description:
By Lizzy Lawrence and Xavier Martinez

To the scientific world, Moderna's cancer vaccine's results proved that a highly personalized, immune-targeting medication can work. To investors, it didn't work well enough.

Details from Moderna's vaccine study showed that, when added to immunotherapy, it reduced the risk of melanoma returning by 42% when compared with immunotherapy alone.

Adil Daud, director of melanoma research at University of California, San Francisco, who worked on the trial, called it "a massive conceptual breakthrough." Scientists have been studying cancer vaccines for decades without success.

Moderna's stock tanked, however, down 19% in the days after the results were prematurely released.

"Investors wanted to see something that was better, something that really pointed to true differentiation," said Evan Seigerman, an analyst with BMO Capital Markets.

The disconnect shows how investors' expectations can outstrip the promise of experimental medicines — even ones scientists say are significant advances in treatment.

While researchers celebrated the results, Wall Street was concerned that they might not be enough to persuade doctors to use what is expected to be a costly new combination. New cancer drugs are introduced at prices of around $400,000 or more a year and this therapy requires more complex manufacturing than most.

Pharma companies are under pressure to show success with new drugs. Moderna must prove that its mRNA vaccine technology has a future outside of infectious diseases, where sales have been declining for years. Merck, a co-developer of the vaccine, must prove it can make up revenue that will be lost when its blockbuster immunotherapy Keytruda goes off patent in about two years.

One problem scientists and Wall Street are puzzling over is that a different study showed using Keytruda alone before surgery appeared to produce a similar result to the vaccine in certain melanoma patients. Merck, which partially funded that study, said the two trials are in different patient populations and can't be compared.

Still, it raised questions for doctors. The cost is "definitely a consideration," said Beth Buchbinder, a medical oncologist at Dana Farber Cancer Institute. "It is a lot easier to, you know, pull a bag of pembrolizumab off the shelf," she said, referring to Keytruda.

Immunotherapies such as Keytruda and Bristol-Myers Squibb's Opdivo have substantially reduced the number of deaths attributed to melanoma since being approved over a decade ago. Their efficacy has created a high bar for treatments that have followed.

Moderna's results did validate a thesis that a cancer vaccine, when added to Keytruda, could be beneficial for some patients. The question is which and exactly how many patients that will be.

"It's quite an individualized discussion," Lisa Tachiki, oncologist at Fred Hutch Cancer Center, said, with questions ranging from how far a cancer has spread to whether a person can tolerate the side effects of immunotherapy.

It is also too soon to tell how much longer patients will live on the Moderna treatment. That data isn't expected for more than a year.

"Are we actually helping our patients live a little longer? Or are we just delaying something that potentially can still be salvaged with immunotherapy at the time of recurrence," Tachiki said.

Clinicians said the vaccine holds promise, particularly for those with less advanced melanoma who don't qualify for immunotherapy before surgery because their tumors are less visible.

Moderna and Merck are studying its potential beyond melanoma, which has been driving investor enthusiasm. The vaccine is already being studied in cancers like kidney and lung and the companies are considering other tumor types.

The drugmakers chose to start with melanoma because it is highly sensitive to immunotherapies, said Eliav Barr, chief medical officer of Merck. But he said the real question is whether the vaccine is "a melanoma product, or is this one of those new cancer interventions that may have benefit in a diverse set of cancers."

Write to Lizzy Lawrence at lizzy.lawrence@wsj.com and Xavier Martinez at xavier.martinez@wsj.com

data.title: 13D Filings — Barrons.com
data.description:
These disclosures are from 13Ds filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 13Ds are filed within 10 days of an entity's attaining more than 5% in any class of a company's securities. Subsequent changes in holdings or intentions must be reported in amended filings. This material is from Oct. 15 through Oct. 21, 2026. Source: VerityData

Activist Filings

Strata Critical Medical (SRTA) Third Point filed an initial 13D regarding its stake in the organ transport and medical logistics company, shifting to the stance of an activist investor from previous disclosures in a passive 13G. Third Point reported that it purchased 170,011 Strata Critical Medical shares from Aug. 31 through Oct. 13 at per share prices ranging from $4.53 to $5.66, after selling 43,500 shares from Aug. 31 through Sept. 30 at $5.11 to $5.66. Third Point said it believes the stock is undervalued and that Strata's business, while strong, isn't of a scale to support its current overhead, adding that management incentive options aren't aligned with creating shareholder value. The firm said Strata should explore strategic alternatives, including a potential sale managed by a reputable investment banking firm.

Following the latest activity, Third Point now owns 5,126,511 Strata Critical Medical shares, or 5.8% of those outstanding. Shares of Strata Critical Medical have lost roughly 4.7% of their value in 2026.

Increases in Holdings

Crescent Energy (CRGY)Independence Energy Aggregator raised its stake in the oil-and-gas producer to 68,655,357 shares. Independence Energy Aggregator did so through the purchase of 40,000,000 Crescent Energy shares on Oct. 8 at a price of $12.50 per share pursuant to an underwritten public offering.

Following the purchase, Independence Energy Aggregator owns a 16.3% stake in Crescent Energy's outstanding stock. Shares of Crescent Energy have gained approximately 57.6% in value in 2026.

Decreases in Holdings

Talos Energy (TALO) Carlos Slim lowered his stake in the oil-and-gas company to 24,500,000 shares. The Mexican billionaire reported that he sold 8,940,000 Talos Energy shares from Oct. 8 through Oct. 13 at per share prices ranging from $16.99 to $17.73.

Following the latest activity, Carlos Slim continues to own a 14.7% stake in Talos Energy's outstanding stock. Slim also disclosed a shift to passive investment intent in a 13G filing on Oct. 20 from previous disclosures in an active 13D. Shares of Talos Energy have gained roughly 59.7% in value in 2026.

Navigator Holdings (NVGS) BW Group lowered its stake in the liquefied-gas shipping company to 3,070,147 shares. BW Group did so through the sale of 988,931 Navigator Holdings shares from Oct. 2 through Oct. 15 at per share prices ranging from $22.00 to $24.66.

Following the latest sales, BW Group continues to own a 4.99% stake in Navigator Holdings' outstanding stock, placing BW Group below the 5% threshold that would require it to report further sales. Shares of Navigator Holdings have gained roughly 22.8% in value in 2026.

data.title: JetBlue creditors working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners, WSJ reports

data.title: S&P 500, Dow Drop As Elevated Oil Prices Stoke Inflation Fears Ahead Of Fed Meeting Next Week — AAPL, AXP, CART, UBER In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 ended Friday 0.5% lower, the Nasdaq 100 was flat, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.2%.
  • The iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped for the third straight week.
  • Apple sold out its limited in-store inventory for the new iPhone Duo.

The S&P 500 and Dow Jones index ended lower on Friday as oil prices spiked amid resurfacing geopolitical concerns, which in turn raised inflation and rate hike worries ahead of the Federal Reserve’s October rate-setting meeting due next week.

The S&P 500 ended Friday 0.5% lower, the Nasdaq 100 was flat, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.2%. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, eased 0.3%.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 0.5%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) fell 1.2%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) ended flat on Friday.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF slumped between 0.5% and 0.7% on Friday as gains in AMD, Micron Tech (MU) and Intel (INTC) offset weakness in Nvidia (NVDA). The broader Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) rose 0.7%.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for SPY, DIA and QQQ was ‘bearish’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

A number of tech equities retreated as market participants weighed how surging corporate debt and elevated interest rates might impact AI-focused companies, particularly following Meta’s expanded capital expenditure forecast. PhillipCapital completely reversed its bearish position, upgrading SpaceX shares from ‘sell’ to ‘buy,’ lauding the company’s advancements in AI or superintelligence.

data.title: Hey, Bud. Don't Anger Your Customers — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Sales of nonalcoholic beer aren't low because it doesn't taste like beer; they're low because it doesn't have any alcohol in it ("This Stock's for You: Buy Bud's 'Diet Coke' Moment," Cover Story, Oct. 14). I've been to Leuven, Belgium, many times. There are lots of bars, and the locals get it. Evidently, execs don't. If the thesis is that nonalcoholic beer is going to save Anheuser-Busch InBev, I'll fade it all day, every day. Here's another idea: Don't anger your customers with your marketing campaigns.

August West On Barrons.com

Tax Income, Not Assets

To the Editor: Taxation of the ultrarich is a difficult subject to agree upon, and probably always will be ("Taxes on the Wealthy Are on the Ballot in Many States. Could It Become a Federal Trend?" Oct. 15). But states need to be careful in how they go about it. If we tax the wealthy based on their assets, does that mean the government goes into their homes and assesses the value of their paintings, cars, and jewelry, or makes them open their safe-deposit boxes to determine the value of the items within? A tax where those with very large incomes pay their fair amount is easier to monitor than to try taxing wealth. We just need to agree upon the definition of a very large income and decide on a fair amount.

Thomas J. Kloepfer Buffalo Grove, Ill.

Dividend Discipline

To the Editor: John D. Rockefeller understood something that many investors have forgotten: Dividends are among the clearest expressions of shareholder ownership ("The S&P 500's Dividend Yield Is at an All-Time Low. What to Do If You're an Income Investor," Oct. 15). From a shareholder's perspective, a corporation is ultimately a machine for converting invested capital into sustainable cash distributions. While buybacks have their place, dividends represent a recurring financial commitment to shareholders. More importantly, dividend increases are among the loudest and clearest signals that management can send about its confidence in future earnings and cash flows. The S&P 500 index's historically low yield doesn't make dividends obsolete. It makes dividend discipline more important than ever.

Brad Thomas Greenville, S.C.

Labor Theory of Value

To the Editor:The propensity for a product or service to decrease in price is inversely proportional to the percentage of labor in said product or service ("Bond Investors See Inflation Cooling. Consumers See Anything But," The Economy, Oct. 16). In other words, because wages have a sticky upward bias, the higher the percentage of labor in a product or service, the less the price will come down when other comprising costs are reduced.

Steven R. Martin Northbrook, Ill.

Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada – October 23, 2026 - TheNewswire – GOAT Industries Ltd. (the “Company” or “GOAT”) (FWB: 26B.F) is pleased to announce, further to its

August 17, 2026 news release, that it and its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, operating as BetSource ("Source Gaming"), have entered into an arm’s length definitive contract revenue assignment agreement dated October 20, 2026 (the "Agreement") with Epoxy AI, LLC ("Epoxy") to acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy (the "Transaction").

The Agreement represents a significant advancement of the Company's previously announced acquisition strategy, providing for the acquisition of all rights to revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under six Epoxy customer contracts with both US Tribal casinos, as well as other well known established casino and sports book operators, in exchange for 11,377,600 GOAT common shares at a deemed price of C$0.25 per share. The Company believes the six customer agreements represent a significant commercial opportunity relative to its existing operations.

Under the Agreement, Source Gaming will acquire the rights to revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under the six customer contracts (the "Contract Revenues") and Epoxy has agreed to assign the underlying customer contracts to Source Gaming within six months following closing, subject to obtaining any required customer consents. Until assignment, Epoxy will continue performing its contractual obligations under the six customer contracts and will hold revenues received under those contracts in trust for Source Gaming and remit them accordingly.

The Transaction supports GOAT's strategy to commercialize its BetSource technology platform across the U.S. Tribal gaming, commercial casino and sports betting markets. data.title: The Plan to Put Super Dogs on the Battlefield of the Future — WSJ
data.description:
By Marcus Weisgerber and Heather Somerville

The U.S. military has long banked on new types of technology to give soldiers an edge on the battlefields of the future. A startup now wants dogs to have a similar advantage, genetically modifying man's best friend to make them run faster, have a keener sense of smell and avoid common genetic conditions.

The idea for a military super dog was conceived by Palmer Luckey, co-founder of defense tech firm Anduril Industries, and Ben Lamm, co-founder of Colossal Biosciences, a bioengineering company that aims to protect endangered species and bring back extinct animals.

Warhound said it has secured $200 million in its first funding round from investors, including In-Q-Tel, the CIA-linked venture-capital firm, and Sequoia Capital. Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia who is leading the firm's investment, is a Pentagon adviser. The funding puts the company's valuation at $1.2 billion, according to PitchBook, a financial research firm.

Based in Texas, the company aims to collect cells from top-performing military and law enforcement dogs, then freeze them and clone the animals, Lamm said. It could then remove deleterious alleles — gene variants that can cause disease or defects — such as those associated with hip dysplasia or other genetic conditions. Eventually, the company aims to improve dogs' sense of smell, speed and agility.

Anduril, which makes weapons and software, will provide eye and hearing protection and body armor for the dogs. Colossal has an equity stake in Warhound, and Lamm sits on its board. Anduril has no stake in the company, and Luckey isn't a board member.

With nearly 90% of the military's working dogs purchased from overseas, Warhound also wants to increase the number of domestically sourced working dogs. "We have to do something to onshore what really is a living supply chain," said David Spirk, the company's chief executive.

The Air Force, which oversees military working dog training for the Pentagon, declined to comment on the new company. Luckey didn't respond to a request for comment.

Warhound said the dogs would be outfitted with the sensing technology. Anduril has developed an AI-powered helmet for humans that is supposed to give soldiers better awareness of their surroundings. The prototype is in early testing stages.

Warhound is starting its work with Belgian Malinois and German Shepherds, but plans to include Labradors and other breeds as well. Its first puppies are expected to be born in the first quarter of 2027.

Lamm began talking to Luckey about working dogs backstage at a conference about a year and a half ago.

Spirk, a former Marine who was the Pentagon's first chief data officer and previously worked at Palantir Technologies, said Warhound has 10 employees and is looking to hire military and law enforcement veterans with K9 experience.

The venture marks a new foray for Luckey, who has branched out from running Anduril, which was recently valued at $90 billion. His bank, Erebor Bank, received a national charter in February and is catering to startups and wealthy individuals.

Last month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth chose Luckey to serve on a committee to study the future of warfare.

Colossal Biosciences has been on a quest to bring back extinct animals, including the woolly mammoth and dodo. The company has been panned by some academics and scientists, who doubt Colossal's claims of scientific breakthroughs and warn that introducing heavily genetically altered creatures can cause dangerous ecological disruption.

Lamm believes advances in AI, quantum computing and bioscience will allow the company to ultimately engineer new forms of life.

Write to Marcus Weisgerber at marcus.weisgerber@wsj.com and Heather Somerville at heather.somerville@wsj.com

data.title: CME live cattle futures unchanged, feeder cattle futures firm
data.description:
Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures were mixed and feeder cattle ticked higher on Friday, as traders positioned ahead of the weekend and the US Department of Agriculture's cattle on feed report, released after the close of the trading session.

CME December live cattle ended the day unchanged at 231.125 cents per pound.

November feeders finished up 1.200 cents at 348.125 cents per pound.

Lack of fresh news and pre-weekend positioning resulted in lackluster trade on Friday, said Karl Setzer, co-founder of Consus Ag Consulting.

But after the session ended, the USDA released its monthly cattle on feed report, showing cattle on feed for slaughter as of October 1 at 100% of last year's numbers and just below the estimate of a Reuters poll of analysts that put them at 100.3% of the previous year.

Meanwhile September placements in feedlots were reported at 88% of last year's numbers, beneath the trade estimate of 92.6% and the lowest for September since 1996.

Wholesale boxed beef prices fell at midday on Friday to $365.79 per hundredweight (cwt) for choice cuts, down $3.68 from the previous day, while select cuts rose $2.29 to $352.69 per cwt.

Beef packer margins fell into the red at the end of the week. Packers lost an average of $4.10 per head, down from profits of $32.15 on Thursday, and $70.90 a week ago, according to livestock marketing advisory service HedgersEdge.

On Friday, 96,000 cattle were slaughtered, down from 102,000 a week ago, according to the USDA.

December lean hog futures (LHZ26) ticked up, ending 0.025 cent higher at 65.575 cents per pound.

The USDA reported prices for pork carcasses fell $1.14 to $74.09 per cwt, while bellies dropped $2.41 to $82.18 per cwt.

On Friday, 462,000 hogs were slaughtered, according to the agency, down from 472,000 a week ago.
